summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Builds real-time computer vision and perception pipelines on NVIDIA Jetson, including a TensorRT-optimized YOLO detector at 92 FPS for vision-guided grasping, plus research in image stitching, denoising, and depth estimation for 3D surface reconstruction.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Designed a custom wavelet bank (alpha-blended sym6+bior3.5) to suppress low-frequency noise; combined with optimized homography stitching and concurrency to achieve a PSNR of 86.
Deployed ZoeDepth monocular depth estimation for crack-depth profiling with ±8% error on 3D surface reconstruction.

experience.title: AI/ML Intern
bullets: Fine-tuned DONUT, an OCR-free transformer vision-language model, with PyTorch and HuggingFace VisionEncoderDecoder on a custom medical billing dataset, raising validation accuracy from 55% to 93%.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Trained YOLOv8n object detection on 1,133 curated and annotated images, reaching 83% mAP@50 on held-out validation; exported to ONNX and TFLite for mobile deployment.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Optimized YOLO object detection with TensorRT on NVIDIA Jetson for real-time visual servoing: 5.2× speedup (56.7→10.9 ms, 17.6→92 FPS vs eager PyTorch), fused with dual ToF range sensing for contact-aware grasping.
Built a vision-guided pick-and-place system across a Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and Jetson+Arduino controller, with multiprocessing multi-camera frame capture.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced VGG16 TorchScript conv layers with custom CUDA C++ kernels (memory coalescing, constant memory, preallocated buffers): 49.2ms vs 73.3ms uncoalesced and 77.5ms CPU, a ~35% speedup at identical accuracy.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving in CARLA
bullets: Auto-generated ~5,000 YOLO and ~3,000 UFLD frames via semantic segmentation with zero manual annotation; trained YOLO11n (mAP50 ~0.85) for a perception stack with zero collisions across 30 vehicles and 10 pedestrians.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects in real time, driving multi-servo PWM on STM32 via interrupt-driven UART commands.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Derived DH tables and forward kinematic chains (0T6) for a 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B; validated against MoveIt and RViz URDF models in ROS 2 Humble; AL5B repeatability <2mm over 10 trials.
